_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Apollo Tyres Ltd (consolidated, Rs crore). FY26 (Mar-2026) is the last reported year; Q1FY27 (Jun-2026, reported 7-Aug-2026) is the last quarter known on 30-Sep-2026. Segment model on the company's three reported geographic segments (external revenue; segment EBITDA = segment result + depreciation, which includes the other income allocated to segments). Consolidated EBITDA = sum of segments less that other income (the 'unallocated' line), which is then added back below EBITDA as other income. No minorities (EPS = profit / 63.51 cr shares).

segments.name: APMEA (India-led)
segments._why: FY27E +15%: standalone (India) revenue +15.6% in Q1FY27 (volume ~+12%: replacement +13%, OEM +10%, exports +15%) and only 3-4% of the 7-9% Q1 price increases flowed into Q1 revenue; ~11% of increases taken by early August with 1-2% in July and ~2% in August, and OEM formula pass-through from Q2 (Q1FY27 call, 7-Aug-2026). Capacity utilisation is in the 90s, so H2 volume growth slows against a GST-boosted base (Q3FY26 +13%, Q4FY26 +14%). FY28E +11%: the Andhra Pradesh expansion (+10,500 PCR and +3,600 TBR tyres a day, ~17-20% more India capacity) starts at end-FY27 and ramps through FY28; price carry-over. FY29E +10%. MOSL standalone FY27E +10.5%; Emkay consolidated +15%.
segments._revWhy: Driver is external revenue itself (after inter-segment sales to Europe).
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA (incl. allocated other income) on external revenue: 16.2% in FY26, 13.4% in FY25, 19.2% in FY24 (FY20-26 median 13.4%, mean 14.9%). It runs ~1.5 pt above standalone EBITDA margin (14.5% in FY26) because export margins earned on inter-segment sales stay in APMEA. Q1FY27 standalone margin 12.0% (13.6%) with raw materials +17% q/q and a further +8% expected in Q2; natural rubber ~Rs225/kg in Q1, ~Rs260+ in Q2, expected to cool from Q3. FY27E 14.2% (standalone ~12.6%: H1 ~12%, H2 ~13.5%); FY28E 15.0% and FY29E 15.3% (standalone ~13.5-14%), back near the FY20-26 average, not the FY24 peak. CRISIL (24-Aug-2026): industry margin 11.5-12% in FY27, 13-13.5% in FY28.

segments.name: Europe (Vredestein, ReifenCom)
segments._why: FY27E +8%: in euros Europe manufacturing revenue was flat in Q1FY27 (EUR147 mn, +0.5%) with low-single-digit volume growth (PCR replacement double-digit; agri tyres down as Enschede closed, 20-25% of agri now bought from offtake partners), but the euro averaged ~10% more in rupees (MOSL: Europe revenue +10.3% in INR terms). We assume ~+2% in euros and ~+6% from the euro's rupee value over the year. FY28E +7%: Hungary PCR capacity 17,000 to 21,000 tyres a day from H2FY27, EU anti-dumping duties on Chinese tyres help the Apollo brand at the lower end (call), ~4% FX/price. FY29E +6%. ReifenCom (distribution, EUR40-43 mn a quarter at 2-3% EBITDA) is inside this segment.
segments._revWhy: Driver is external revenue itself (in rupees).
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 13.0% in FY26, 13.6% in FY25, 15.2% in FY24 (FY22-26 average 14.3%); company basis (excl. ReifenCom) 14.0% in FY26 and 8.9% in Q1FY27, ~11% without the Enschede/Hungary cost overlap (CFO). Enschede stopped production in Jun-2026; benefits from H2FY27 (management); 'high teens' is the full-year aspiration once the footprint is right. FY27E 12.0% (H1 ~9.5%, H2 ~14%); FY28E 14.0%; FY29E 15.0%: below management's high-teens aim because Europe raw materials lag (only 3-4% of a needed ~10% price increase taken by Aug-2026) and the market is flat.

segments.name: Others (Americas, corporate)
segments._why: Americas sales (US weak: dealer inventories not clearing, Q1FY27 call) and corporate entities; 4% of revenue.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA 10.1% of external revenue in FY26 (FY23-25: 21-30%, swollen by corporate income and inter-segment margins that are not stable). We hold 10%.

_unallocLabel: Other income included in segment results (moved below EBITDA)
_unallocWhy: Segment results include other income (FY26 Rs133 cr: segment EBITDA Rs4,277 cr vs company EBITDA Rs4,143 cr). We take it out of EBITDA here and add the same amount back as other income below, so reported EBITDA and PBT are not double counted.
_capexWhy: Guidance: ~Rs3,000-3,500 cr in FY27 (Q4FY26 call, May-2026: Rs3,500 cr, ~Rs3,000 cr of it in India; MOSL after Q1: ~Rs3,000 cr reiterated); Q1FY27 Rs650 cr. The board approved Rs5,800 cr for the Andhra Pradesh plant over FY27-29 (Feb-2026: +10,500 PCR and +3,600 TBR tyres a day at ~Rs17 cr per tonne-day); FY28 'might be even higher than Rs3,000 cr', FY29 tapering (Q3FY26 call). Maintenance ~Rs700 cr a year. FY26 cash capex Rs1,355 cr (Screener investing cash flow basis).
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs1,543 cr (incl. right-of-use assets) = 4.75% of average gross block (Rs32,508 cr, Screener basis, FY25-26); Q1FY27 Rs391 cr (Rs1,564 cr annualised). The engine depreciates new capex at once and holds CWIP (Rs1,077 cr at Mar-26, up from Rs435 cr) flat, while much of the AP capex is CWIP until end-FY27; 4.6% offsets that timing. FY27E Rs1,638 cr vs MOSL Rs1,615 cr.
_treasuryWhy: Apollo has net debt (Rs3,675 cr of borrowings incl. Rs1,044 cr of leases vs Rs1,044 cr of cash at Mar-26), so the engine's treasury is negative and earns nothing; interest on the ~Rs1,000 cr of cash is inside other income below.
_otherIncomeWhy: Built from FY26 note B24 (Rs133 cr): interest on bank deposits Rs14 cr and other interest (incl. on a government grant) Rs23 cr, foreign-exchange gains Rs66 cr, profit on asset sales Rs19 cr, miscellaneous Rs10 cr, investment income Rs1 cr. Recurring core ~Rs50 cr (interest and misc.); FX gains recur while the rupee weakens. FY27E Rs125 cr = Q1 Rs58 cr (company basis, before the Rs23.5 cr exceptional gain that Screener adds) + ~Rs22 cr a quarter (MOSL: Rs21-23 cr a quarter). FY28-29E ~Rs110-115 cr. TTM-Jun-26 on the company basis Rs148 cr.
_interestWhy: FY26 finance costs Rs391 cr (AR; Screener Rs419 cr) after borrowings fell from Rs2,977 cr to Rs2,632 cr (ex-leases); Q1FY27 Rs92 cr. Capex of Rs6,500 cr over FY27-28 against ~Rs4,000 cr of operating cash means borrowing again ('we will be a net borrower', CFO): +Rs40 cr in FY27E and +Rs50 cr more in FY28E. MOSL FY27E Rs435 cr.
_taxWhy: India moved to the 25.2% regime from FY27 (Finance Act 2026); Europe ~20% (Q4FY26 call). Q1FY27 25.4%. FY26 was −5% on a ~Rs570 cr deferred-tax write-back.
_payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs6.0 a share (interim Rs3.5, final Rs2.5) = 22% of EPS before one-offs (Rs26.7) and 28% of reported EPS; FY25 Rs5.0. Policy: at least 20% of standalone profit.

dcf._betaWhy: A cyclical, raw-material-driven margin, a European business with high fixed costs and modest net debt (~0.4x EBITDA): beta 1.0 gives a 12.5% cost of equity, used as the discount rate (debt is ~6% of market value, so WACC would be ~12.1%).
dcf._tgWhy: Indian tyre demand grows with the vehicle parc and freight plus price; Europe is flat. 5.5% nominal (house range 5-6%).
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~9% to 7.5% over 12 years: India 9-10%, Europe 3-4%.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 14.5%, near the FY20-26 median (14%) and below FY24's 17.6%.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades from 5.8% of revenue (FY29E) to 5.5% (FY20-26 average ~5.5%); depreciation 5.3% of revenue (FY26 5.4%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Natural rubber falls back towards ₹200/kg from Q3FY27 while the 11-16% price increases stick (the industry's best margins come in a falling raw-material cycle, CFO); India keeps double-digit volume on the new AP capacity; Europe reaches management's mid-teens margin by FY28 as Enschede's costs go and Hungary ramps up.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Rubber and crude-linked inputs stay high and a weak monsoon and fuel prices slow truck and farm demand; price increases slip as competitors and Chinese imports undercut; Europe stays flat with agri volumes lost to the offtake transition, so the margin stays near Q1FY27's 12% and the ₹5,800 cr AP capex earns little before FY29.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Apollo: P/E on one-year-forward EPS (MOSL 16x FY28E, 7-Aug-2026; Emkay 18x Jun-28E, 9-Aug-2026). Multiple derived in APOLLOTYRE.ctx.js and written by APOLLOTYRE.val.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: The second street method (ICICI Direct 7x FY28E; Nomura 6.3x FY28F earlier): values the operating business and deducts net debt.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 12-year FCFF, Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 5.5%, less net debt.
